content.value_statement: Cloudflare One projects span identity, routing, endpoint, and traffic controls that can fail when designed separately. This skill connects those decisions with validation and rollback guidance.
actual_capabilities: Classifies requests as architecture, configuration, troubleshooting, migration, or review work.
Collects requirements for Access, Gateway, device clients, tunnels, identity, DLP, CASB, and site connectivity.
Explains product responsibilities, policy evaluation, routing dependencies, and deployment prerequisites.
Produces staged change plans with assumptions, tests, rollout scope, validation, and rollback steps.
Guides troubleshooting from logs and traffic paths toward the responsible policy, route, or configuration.
Directs users to current Cloudflare documentation before relying on exact fields, limits, identifiers, or interface paths.
limitations: It does not replace current Cloudflare documentation or API schemas.
It requires account context and tool access to inspect or change existing resources.
It does not provide migration planning from competing vendors.
It cannot guarantee feature availability because plans, interfaces, and product behavior can change.

use_cases.title: Plan a Zero Trust rollout
use_cases.description: Create a phased architecture covering identity, private applications, device enrollment, traffic inspection, testing, and rollback.

use_cases.title: Diagnose private access failures
use_cases.description: Trace device routing, DNS, tunnel health, origin reachability, Access policy decisions, and relevant logs.

use_cases.title: Review production policy changes
use_cases.description: Check prerequisites, evaluation order, affected users, pilot scope, validation cases, and recovery steps before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Identify the right Cloudflare One components
prompt_templates.prompt: We need to protect [applications] for [users and devices]. Ask essential questions, then recommend relevant Cloudflare One components and explain each responsibility.

prompt_templates.title: Plan private application access
prompt_templates.prompt: Design access to [private applications] from [managed or unmanaged devices]. Cover identity, routing, DNS, connectors, policies, pilot scope, tests, and rollback.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot a failed connection
prompt_templates.prompt: Users cannot reach [destination] through [connection method]. Build a traffic path, list evidence to collect, rank likely failure points, and define next tests.

prompt_templates.title: Review a production change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed Cloudflare One change: [change]. Check current documentation, dependencies, policy order, blast radius, validation, observability, and rollback before recommending approval.

output_examples.input: Plan employee access to private web applications in two data centers.
output: Assumptions and open decisions covering identity, devices, DNS, routes, and compliance.
Target architecture using redundant connectors, private routes, Access applications, reusable policies, and device profiles.
Pilot phases, success criteria, log checks, failure tests, and rollback actions.

output_examples.input: Explain why enrolled devices resolve a private hostname but cannot connect.
output: Traffic path from the device client through route selection, Cloudflare, the connector, and the origin.
Checks for split tunnel entries, hostname routes, resolver policies, tunnel health, origin reachability, and Access decisions.
A prioritized next test based on the first missing log or route result.

output_examples.input: Review a broad TLS inspection and DLP rollout before production.
output: Prerequisite review for root certificate deployment, pinned applications, exceptions, DLP profiles, and payload logging.
A disabled or pilot-scoped rollout with representative test traffic and false-positive monitoring.
Go-live gates, owner assignments, monitoring signals, and rollback steps.

best_practices: Retrieve current Cloudflare documentation before naming limits, identifiers, request fields, or exact interface paths.
Inspect existing account resources and dependencies before proposing changes.
Pilot risky policies with explicit tests, monitoring, approval, and rollback.
anti_patterns: Do not guess category identifiers, application identifiers, policy fields, or request bodies.
Do not enable broad production controls before testing representative users, devices, applications, and exceptions.
Do not treat tunnel health alone as proof of working private connectivity.

faq.question: Does this skill make Cloudflare account changes?
faq.answer: It can guide changes when suitable account tools are available. It should inspect existing resources and request approval before broad production actions.

faq.question: Can it design both Access and Gateway policies?
faq.answer: Yes. It distinguishes application authorization from traffic inspection and explains when a requirement needs both products.

faq.question: Can it troubleshoot private network access?
faq.answer: Yes. It reviews device routing, DNS, tunnel routes, connector health, origin reachability, policies, and logs.

faq.question: Does it support device client deployments?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers enrollment rules, device profiles, split tunnels, managed settings, service token enrollment, and coexistence concerns.

faq.question: Can it plan migrations from another vendor?
faq.answer: No. Use the separate cloudflare-one-migrations skill for migration planning from other vendors.

faq.question: How does it handle changing Cloudflare features?
faq.answer: It directs the agent to retrieve current documentation or API schemas before giving exact configuration details.
